references.text: God is referred to as 'the Rock' (צוּר), a title that emphasizes his strength and reliability as Israel's protector.
David calls the Lord his Rock (צוּר), reflecting the same image of God as a safe refuge and savior.
Isaiah refers to Israel having forgotten their saving God and their rock of refuge, a direct echo of the accusation in Deuteronomy.
God reminds Israel that he formed them and that they should not forget him, which corresponds with the theme of forgetting God who created them.
Isaiah urges Israel to look to the rock from which they were hewn and remembers Abraham and Sarah who gave birth to them—an image of God's role as their origin.
Job describes those who forget God, reflecting the same act of forgetting the Creator as in Deuteronomy.
Jeremiah accuses Israel of having forgotten the Lord for countless days, paralleling the accusation of forgetting God who gave them birth.
Hosea says that Israel has forgotten their Maker, a direct echo of the accusation in Deuteronomy about forgetting God who gave them birth.
